# Rules: Automations

**Covers:** Workflows, schedules, rules, watchers, goals, webhooks: `workflows/`, `scheduling/`, `reflex/`, `sentinels/`, `triggers/`, `webhooks/`, `goals/`, `motivation/`.

How to use this file: read the contents list, then read only the entries your change touches (each line gives the line number where the full text starts). The rules that apply to every change are in the root `CLAUDE.md`. To add a rule, see "Adding a rule" there.

## Rules

- **A step that RAISES is a failed step, and a result is written when it
  LANDS** (v1.231.0, audit Wave 5, AE3/AE4). The tool branch of the
  workflow engine caught `Exception` and returned a failed output; the agent
  branch beside it caught only `CancelledError`, so a session that re-raised
  a provider error ("fleet down at 3am") escaped the attempt loop —
  no retry, no `on_failure`, no `workflow.step_completed`, a silent halt —
  and outputs were persisted once per BATCH, so a crash mid-parallel-group
  dropped every finished member and Resume re-delivered them. Two sibling
  branches that handle the same failure must handle it the same way, and a
  record that claims to make resume honest must be written per step, not
  per batch (`_exec_step` writes its own output; `_update_record` snapshots
  the dict because siblings now mutate it). `tests/test_workflow_engine_v1231.py`.
  ORDER (v1.323.1): every async write goes through `WorkflowEngine._persist`,
  which stamps it on the loop; `_update_record` (under one process-wide lock)
  drops `outputs`/`session_ids` from a write older than one already committed
  for that run — a worker thread delayed by SQLite's busy back-off once put a
  crashed run's `{Tell}` back over the resume's final record (Tests gate red,
  `KeyError: 'Work'`). Never add a bare `to_thread(self._update_record, …)`;
  `tests/test_workflow_write_order_v13231.py`.

- **A cancel goes to the task's OWN loop, and a fire that did not happen is
  written where the user reads** (v1.231.0, audit Wave 5, AE2/AE9/AE11/
  AE12). A schedule fire runs under `asyncio.run` on the APScheduler thread;
  `task.cancel()` from any other thread neither wakes that loop's selector
  nor is thread-safe, so Cancel landed when the model call returned on its
  own. `cancel_session` compares `task.get_loop()` with the running loop and
  uses `loop.call_soon_threadsafe(task.cancel)` across loops (the cancel
  route is a sync `def`, so every route cancel is cross-thread). The
  scheduler's silent outcomes — APScheduler's 1 s default misfire grace
  turned a PC asleep at 03:00 into a WARNING in its own logger; a skipped
  overlap likewise; a fire the app was closed for left `next_run` in the
  past under an `ok` — are now rows: `misfire_grace_time=300` on recurring
  jobs, an `EVENT_JOB_MAX_INSTANCES | EVENT_JOB_MISSED` listener, and
  `start()` reconciling recurring rows to `missed` WITHOUT firing. Two traps
  in `scheduling/service.py`: cron/interval `next_run` is stored as the
  scheduler zone's wall clock while `last_run` is UTC (SQLite drops tzinfo),
  so each is read on its own clock; and `misfire_grace_time=None` means
  UNLIMITED, not default. Every trigger is handed the scheduler's zone —
  APScheduler re-resolves tzlocal per trigger, so a UTC fallback on the
  scheduler alone would have booted the daemon and then aborted `start()` on
  the first cron task. `tests/test_scheduler_trust_v1231.py`.

  words with the cron kept, anything odd as stored; `query` keeps matching
  name/work; `LIST_MAX` 50). `records._record_tools_named` offers it FIRST
  whenever a schedule is named, and it is in `_RECORD_READERS` (a question
  about schedules offers only it). `ScheduleUpdateTool` / `ScheduleDeleteTool`

  `tests/test_schedule_list_v1486.py` (9 mutations, all red), the two
  calendar-removal tests in `test_calendar_link_lookup_v1484.py`. Same release:
  `settings/trigger._EXTRA_REFERENCES` reads "stop it / the app / Jarvis

- **Chat can make a plain TASK schedule** (v1.483.0). `scheduling/tools.

- **A stored schedule time means the scheduler's zone everywhere, and an interval is anchored to its last run** (v1.499.3 review). The catch-up read a naive `run_at` as UTC while the trigger read it as local: a restart fired a future one-time task hours early. An `IntervalTrigger` with no start slid forward on every restart and never fired; it now starts one interval after `last_run` (or `created_at`). The calendar maps Windows zone names (`tzlocal.windows_tz`), expands simple RRULEs (claimed as `UID@<start>Z`) and skips, in words, what it cannot read. Reflex rules fence the signal text (`wrap_untrusted`, one-pass `_render`). Pins: `tests/test_review_fixes_daemon_v1499_3.py`.

- **A workflow step is bounded, a run that cannot go on ends with a result, and an OK can be kept on a schedule or a workflow** (v1.505.0, north-star plan group 5).
  TOOL STEPS. A workflow's tool step passes `deadline_s=_tool_deadline(config)`
  (the runtime's and both chat lanes' one helper) and runs as its own task
  in the engine's `_TOOL_CALLS` table, keyed by run id.
  `workflows.engine.cancel_tool_steps(run_id)` is what the cancel route
  calls after setting `cancelling`: it stops the CALL (the registry's cancel
  path ledgers it) and the step returns `cancelled` with a result. Do not
  cancel the run's driver task instead: a scheduled workflow's driver is
  registered nowhere, and a cancelled driver writes no result.
  THE DRIVER. `run_record`, `resume_after_answer` and `resume_interrupted`
  go through `_settled_on_raise`: an exception outside a step writes
  `failed` (`cancelled` when the run was cancelling) with its reason, in a
  shielded task off the loop, publishes `workflow.completed` with `reason`,
  and re-raises. A cancellation is NOT settled (a restart leaves the row for
  the boot reconcile). Every `_get_record` read is `asyncio.to_thread`.
  STANDING OKS. `core/grants.SCOPE_KINDS` has `schedule` and `workflow`,
  read from the run's origin (`ORIGIN_SCOPES`, `runtime.grant_scopes`);
  precedence is schedule, workflow, agent, project, goal, chat, so "Always"
  on a scheduled run is kept on the SCHEDULE. The ask's event carries
  `always_scope` for those two only; `approvals.note_always` keeps
  `can_always`, `always_scope` and `args_hash` beside the ask so
  `routes/sessions._waiting_on` (the run's page) and
  `GET /chat/approvals/pending` (the bell) both offer it. A new surface that
  shows a run's ask passes `always_scope` to `alwaysLabel`. The grant is the
  existing kind: exact arguments, 30 days, never "never", and the deny floor
  and a definition's deny stand. `GET /schedules` and `GET /workflows` rows
  carry `standing_grants`; `grant_revoke` resolves a schedule or workflow
  name; `SchedulerService.remove` and `WorkflowStore.remove` call a hook the
  platform sets to `GrantStore.revoke_scope` (a removed schedule's OKs go
  with it). A schedule that runs a custom agent passes `agent_name`.
  Pins: `tests/test_north_star_{workflow_tool_step,workflow_driver,schedule_grants}_v1505.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/north-star-held-oks-v1505.test.tsx` and the bell case
  in `bell-outcomes-v13580.test.tsx`.

- **A workflow's tool step reads the tool's own "ask every time" check, and is refused when it asks** (v1.520.0, third review PG2).
  `WorkflowEngine._run_tool_step` calls `_own_check_refusal` (the lanes'
  one reader, `tools/base.spend_checks_for`, with no posture: a workflow has
  no "Don't ask"). A check that asks makes the step fail in words through
  `registry.invoke(deny_reason=, deny_label=OWN_CHECK_LABEL)`, so the ledger
  has the refusal and the tool never runs. No standing approval covers it
  ("Always for this workflow" is never offered for a call whose own check
  asks, in any lane), and a tool step has no way to wait: refused, never
  parked. The sentences are `own_check_refusal_words` and
  `tier_refusal_words` (an ask-tier tool names an Agent step; nothing
  advises "auto-approve"). Pin: `tests/test_third_plan_g17_workflow_step.py`.

- **Anything set up from a chat reports into that chat through ONE field and ONE writer: `chat_thread_id` on the record, `chat_delivery.report_to_chat`** (idea 39, phase 39-a; master plan R1.1, D-39.1 to D-39.3).
  THE FIELD. `chat_thread_id: str = ""` on `ScheduledTaskRecord`, `SentinelRecord`, `GoalContractRecord`, `WorkflowRunRecord`, `NightTaskRecord` (additive; NULL reads ""; indexed, `core.db._HOT_INDEXES` for an older table). Stamped only by a CHAT door, through `chat_delivery.report_chat_for`: `ToolContext.thread_id`, or for a NEW chat's first turn (it carries no thread id until the first save names the chat) the chat the page linked the turn to (`chat_of_turn`); a record made before that link waits (`note_pending_report`) and `POST /chat/turns/{id}/thread` stamps it (`stamp_linked_reports`, only while it still reports nowhere). Then `stampable_chat` (a saved chat; never a coding session or a phone thread (`owner == "daemon"`) until 39-c: `_takes_reports`, the same rule `set_report_target` applies): `schedule_create`, `sentinel_add`, `workflow_run`, `night_task_add`, and `POST /goals` `chat_thread_id` (the chat's goal card). A page that makes the same record stamps nothing. Changed only through `chat_delivery.set_report_target` (`POST /reports/target {kind, id, thread_id}`, "" = Stop reporting, answers `previous` for the Undo; `schedule_update` / `sentinel_update` / `goal_update` (a goal from chat) `report_here` with the record's own Undo, which puts the chat back only for a `report_here` change (`REPORT_CHANGE_MARK`) or a delete, never for a pause or a timing change; a tool CHECKS the chat first and APPLIES `report_here` only after the rest of the call is valid, putting the rest back if it then fails). `only_if=` is compare-and-clear: a gone chat clears a link only while it still names that chat, and a report's own Stop reporting sends the chat it is in (`POST /reports/target` `only_if`; "It reports to another chat now." otherwise, except that a stop on a record that reports nowhere already is ok with `changed` False: it says "Reports stopped." and a gone chat clears nothing). A later idea that adds a source (05-a's `ReflexRule`, 39-c's phone) adds its table to `_record_class` / `REPORT_TARGET_KINDS`, never a second field or writer.
  THE WRITER. `report_to_chat(platform, thread_id, report)` is BLOCKING (callers on the loop `asyncio.to_thread`) and never raises. It builds ONE line (`report_line`: `reportFrom {kind, name, id, href, outcome, runId}`, `reportKey`, `reportFold`), composed by code: the lead from the kind and name, the verdict word from the ledger (`outcome.run_ending` or the source's own record, never the model's closing words), the words cut at `REPORT_MAX_CHARS`. `chat_append` keeps the five `report*` keys in `LINE_KEYS`, treats `report:<key>` (and every key in `reportSeen`) as a repeat, and REPLACES the day's line of the same record in place (`reportFold` = kind, id, local date; `reportCount`): one line a day per record, unless the user wrote after that line (then the report is a new line, which later reports that day fold into). A watcher is never folded (`REPORT_NOT_FOLDED`): it writes at most once an hour, the rest wait on the row (`report_at`, `report_pending_json`) and join the next one. `unarchive=False`: a report leaves an archived chat archived and rings `report.arrived` (titles only); a chat that is gone clears the field, notes it on the row (`note_gone_on_row`: a schedule's `last_detail`, a night task's or a workflow run's notes) and rings `report.chat_gone`. A run's report re-reads the record's field when it ends (`report_target_of`), so Stop reporting pressed meanwhile holds it.
  THE SOURCES. A schedule's task fire carries `chat_thread_id`, `report_from` and (for a Local only chat) `local_only` in its run options, so the RUN's own ending writes the report (`line_for_session`, durable through the finalizers and the boot reconcile; no `panelWho`); a fire with no run of its own (refused, a workflow schedule, skipped) is reported by `_fire` once (`schedule:<id>:<fire time>`); a stop writes nothing. A goal's try carries `report_from.by = "source"` (the run writes nothing) and `GoalEngine._report_try` writes one report after the checks; a try refused for its budget, its breaker or its tools writes one too (`_report_refused`, once a day per reason). `workflow.completed`, the goal's try events and a run's `session.completed` carry `chat_thread_id`, so the bell and the tray open that chat. A workflow run writes one at each of its three endings (`WorkflowEngine._report_end`). A night task writes one from `finish_task` (`report_ended`) with its checks (`report_checks`: the morning facts' test verdict and files changed); a Local only task leaves its branch and notes out of a chat that is not Local only and names itself `LOCAL_ONLY_TITLE` in the bell (`notice_name`). The chat's goal card says Reports here only when the answer's `goal.reports_to` is set. A continuation drops `report_from`; a rerun drops only a `by: source` one.
  THE MODEL. The page labels a report `[Report from your <kind> "<name>", written when it ran. Not your words.]` (`lib/reports.reportRequestLabel`) and `chat_refs.fence_agent_lines` fences what follows (`REPORT_LINE_PREFIX`) in both lanes before the history planner. The @-agent lane is the page's THIRD way of sending the chat to a model: `lib/panelHistory.panelHistoryOf` labels a report the same way, and `AgentThreads._speaker_line` says it as `_REPORT_SPEAKER` (never "Iron Jarvis") with the same fence, in a local seat's transcript and a remote's rows; a fourth way gets both. A report carries its run's receipt (a schedule's run, a goal's try: `GoalEngine._try_receipt`), and a workflow's report carries `chat_delivery.low_trust_receipt` when any step ran at low trust. The recap pass reads a daemon-written line's `receipt.trust` too and labels a report as the record's (`lines_of` `report`); a referenced chat's snapshot labels it "Report from your <kind> (not Jarvis)"; `change_claims` never counts a report as Jarvis's own earlier claim (`_NOT_JARVIS_PREFIXES`). A watcher's report says a suggestion waits only when that sweep made one. `sentinel_add` says the one step while watchers are off. Not built in 39-a: a Chat › Code session's reports (39-b starts one from chat). Pins: `tests/test_leap39a_report_writer.py`, `tests/test_leap39a_sources.py`, `tests/test_leap39a_report_is_data.py`, `tests/test_leap39a_local_only.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/leap-39a-report-line.test.tsx`.

- **Every start goes through ONE hub, and a rule's folder, download, agent, folder of work, hourly limit and "Always" live on the rule** (idea 05, phase 05-a; master plan R1.3, D-05.1 to D-05.3).
  THE HUB. `triggers/starts.StartHub.signal(kind, context=None, *, fields=None)` is the one entry for every kind (`START_KINDS`; `phone` is stored as `comm`). It calls the router EXACTLY as the caller used to: `fields` go to the kind's own entry point (`on_webhook(slug, body)`, `on_calendar(...)`, `on_slack(...)`, `on_email(...)`, `on_comm(text)`), a built `context` to `on_signal(source, ctx)`, `on_file` or `on_download`; then its waiters (`add_waiter`, for 08-c and 09-c; a waiter reads, never starts). Callers reach it by `starts.hub_for(router)` (the router owns `start_hub`; a test that swaps the router swaps the hub). Never call a router entry point from a caller again: `tests/test_leap05a_start_hub.py::test_nothing_in_the_app_calls_the_router_past_the_hub` reads every file of the app (the Undo's webhook handler, `records._inbound_handler`, was missed once). The context builders (`comm_context`, `email_context`, `calendar_context`, `slack_context`, `file_context`, `download_context`) live in `reflex/router.py`, read by the router and the hub alike.
  A FILE RULE. `ReflexRule.start_json {path, glob, per_file}`; its folder is watched by a `rule`-mode `SentinelRecord` (`mode`, `rule_id`), never a second scanner. `reflex_create` makes the rule and the watcher in one call (`records.sync_rule_watcher`; refused in words before anything is made by `SentinelService.check_watch`), the store's `on_removed` hook (registered weakly by the platform, the v1.505.1 lesson) removes the watcher and revokes the rule's grants, and `restore_reflex` brings the watcher back on an Undo. `SentinelService.check_rule` returns only NEW files whose `[mtime, size]` (`watcher.stat_scanner`) is the same on two scans; the baseline is taken when the watcher is MADE or its folder changes (`starts.take_baseline`, so a file dropped right after starts the rule), never at the loop's first scan; a file the rule's own runs wrote (`starts.own_output`: its path AND bytes in the Undo journal of a run with `options.rule_id`) is decided and starts nothing (a file a program the run started wrote is not told apart: the Handbook says so); every file a journal row lists counts (`starts._written_files` reads a row by its shape: a single `path`, `apply_patch`'s `files`, a `paths` list with its `sha256` map as `stack_apply` and the registry's created files write it, `pdf_split`'s `dir` + `outputs` + `hashes`), so a new tool that writes many files records them in one of those shapes (`test_the_many_files_a_split_or_a_sort_writes_in_its_folder_start_nothing`); `mark_rule_seen` marks a file seen only once `rule_fire` (`starts.file_rule_fire`, the watcher's thread waiting on the daemon's loop, bounded) DECIDED it, so a paused rule's files wait and a restart starts nothing twice; at most `RULE_FIRES_PER_SCAN` (20) a scan. One sweep of a rule watcher at a time (`_poll_rule`'s `_rule_sweeps`: a second sweep leaves it to the first, `test_two_sweeps_at_once_start_one_file_once`); a start that outlasts the wait is kept in `under_way` (path, time and size: a new file of the same name starts again) and marks its files seen when it ENDS (`mark_seen`, on its own thread); the page's Check now (`POST /sentinels/poll`) sweeps `suggest_only`. The loop arms when `sentinels_enabled` is on OR a rule-mode watcher exists (`has_rule_watchers`, read at arm time), and polls `rules_only` while suggestion watchers are off; a file-rule change re-arms it (`records.rearm_folder_watching`). A rule that is off or gone decides its files (left alone). A rule's own watcher is changed only with its rule: `sentinel_update`, `sentinel_delete`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /sentinels/{name}` refuse it in words (`starts.rule_owns_words`; 409 on the routes), and `snap_sentinel` / `restore_sentinel` carry `mode` and `rule_id`. Chat: a folder arrival, a watched folder with work, or a download said as a standing request (`setup_words.files_arrive_in_folder` / `watch_and_act` / `download_finishes`) arms `reflex_create`; `sentinel_add` only when a watcher is named; the `watcher_suggests` line says which does what (`tests/test_leap05a_rule_from_chat.py::test_the_sentence_arms_the_rule_and_the_model_is_told_which_does_the_work`).
  A DOWNLOAD RULE. `starts.download_handler` (an event-bus handler) reads only a VERIFIED `browser.download_completed` (`local_path` present) and sends the local path, name and `site_of` the address (never a query) to the hub; `start_json.match_site` filters by host (`store.site_matches`). `download` is in `OUTSIDE_SOURCES` (D-05.2: careful mode), and a FILE rule on a folder named Downloads starts carefully too (`router.watches_downloads`, read by `_signal_trust` and `starts.describe`).
  OUTSIDE WORDS. `{file}`, `{path}`, `{site}` are FENCED (a file's name is chosen by whoever made it), `{folder}` is one line; the default task of a file or download rule fences the location. `tests/test_leap05a_outside_text.py`.
  THE RULE'S RUN. `_run_session` resolves `agent_name` through `agents/resolve.resolve_for_unattended` (the schedule's fire uses the same helper now: one place says what a name means; its words for a schedule are byte-identical), passes `workspace_root`, and carries `options.rule_id` (`router.RULE_OPTION`) plus idea 39's `chat_thread_id` / `report_from {kind: rule}` / `local_only` (`rule_report_options`). `ReflexRule.chat_thread_id` is in `chat_delivery._record_class` / `REPORT_TARGET_KINDS` (Stop reporting on the row; an Undo of a change never re-points it, only a recreate does).
  THE HOURLY LIMIT. `max_fires_per_hour` (12, D-05.3) counts unattended STARTS (`recent_starts_json`): the router's gate COUNTS a start as it lets it through (`start_gate(reserve=True)` under the process-wide `_GATE_LOCK`, one read-and-write, so a burst of signals cannot all pass), and a start that then fails gives its slot back (`release_start`); never count after the run is made. The next signal at the limit PAUSES the rule (`start_gate`: `paused_at`, `paused_reason` "Paused: it started 12 times in an hour.") and answers `held` (no `last_error`, no failure notice, no `reflex.fired`). `reflex.paused` is published at most once a day per rule (`note_told`); the bell's row opens `/reflex?rule=<id>` where **Resume** (`POST /reflex/rules/{id}/resume`, also turning an OFF rule on; a PATCH of a rule that is already on never resumes it, though the page's form sends `enabled`) and **Keep it paused** (`.../keep-paused`: the rule is switched off) wait. An Undo puts a pause back and never lifts one: `snap_reflex` carries `paused_at`/`paused_reason` and `restore_reflex` re-pauses a rule whose snapshot was paused (the Undo of a resume, of a removal), and leaves a later pause alone (`test_undo_puts_a_rules_pause_back_and_never_lifts_a_pause_that_came_later`). Removing a rule revokes its "Always for this rule" grants and an Undo does not bring them back (`reflex_delete`'s description says so). Not sent to the phone or the tray. Run now (attended) is never held or counted. Inject `router.clock` in tests. Chat reads a rule's state through `app_search` (`guide.tools._rule_blurb`: its When and Do, off, or paused and how it starts again, and its last failure).

(`Rhythm.words`), every line from the record (`collect.offer_item`).

- **An If or a For each is run by the ONE step executor, its steps' outputs are keyed by their path, and a block that would run wrongly is refused before the run exists** (v1.595.0, idea 09, phase 09-a; master plan R2.20, D-09.1).
  THE ENGINE. `STEP_KINDS` has `if` and `for_each` (`BLOCK_KINDS`); `Step` has `condition`, `steps`, `else_steps`, `over`, `max_items`, `parallel`; `step_to_dict` writes them for a block only (every other step is the same ten fields), and `load_workflow` REFUSES an unknown kind by name (`UnknownStepKind`, `unknown_kind_words`; the run route answers 400 with it, a schedule's fire raises `_ScheduleRefused` with it), never coerces it to an agent step. Every step goes through `WorkflowEngine._exec_any(ctx, frame, i)`: a step of the workflow's own list is called exactly as before; a block runs `_exec_for_each` / `_exec_if`, whose steps run through `_run_list` (batches, the cancel read before each, an ask's `_AskPark` going up to the driver) and the same `_exec_step` with `key` (the path: `Each file/3/Read total`, `Check/then/Ask`, items counted from 1), `view` (`_scope_view`: the record, then each block's item and its own list's steps by plain name), `at` and `park_index`. So "a finished step is never run again" makes resume work with no new mechanism: a For each writes its list into its own output (`status: running`, `list`, `found`) BEFORE the first item, a resume walks that list (a folder that changed since is not read again), a settled item's row (`done`/`failed`) is never run again, and an If records `took` before its lane runs and never decides again. A parked ask inside a block writes `waiting_json.step` = its key and `at` = its definition's locator (`step_at`); `resume_after_answer` folds the answer under the key (a failed fold is marked `folded`, so the block reads it as the step's result) and drives the run again FROM THE BLOCK'S index, not past it. `settle_open_blocks` ends a block left `running` (the driver's end, and the cancel route for a parked run). A step inside a block publishes its events with `block` (the chat card skips them).
  THE ROLLUP. A For each's output is `{done, failed, skipped (not run), total, data: [{n, label, status, summary}]}` and its summary is `rollup_words` ("14 of 14 done", "12 of 14 done, 2 failed"); a settled item's steps are cut to `_MAX_ITEM_SUMMARY` (300) with no `data` (a 200-item run's record stays under 160 KB, asserted). A failed item follows the block's `on_failure`: halt stops the block (the run fails), skip goes on and the block ends `failed` + `handled` (the run "Part failed"); an inner step's own skip makes the item failed but never stops the block. BOUNDS: D-09.1 `max_items` 200 (the next item stops the run with `items_bound_words`, `bound: True`, which no skip lifts), `MAX_STEP_RUNS` 2,000 per run (`STEP_RUNS_WORDS`), `parallel` 1 to `MAX_PARALLEL` (4), nesting 3. A folder is listed through `_run_tool_step` on `list_folder` (its `pattern` arg and `entries` data are this phase's; the permission tier, the own check and the ledger apply), files only, by name; a list `from` a step's data is at most 8,000 characters of JSON (the step data bound: a bigger one stops with words). Items from a folder or from `{{Trigger}}` are `outside` and FENCED in an agent step's task like `{{Trigger}}`.
  THE CHECK. `workflows/logic.py` (no model, no `eval`): `{left, op, right}` or one level of `all`/`any`, ops `logic.OPS`; numbers read tolerantly (`read_number`: "5,000.00", "(250)"; "5.000,00" is not one), a side that is not a number for a number op raises `ConditionError` and the If FAILS with "could not decide: … Nothing was guessed."; `matches` is a wildcard (`logic.wildcard_match`: only * and ?, a [ is plain text; never `fnmatch` directly, pinned by `test_square_brackets_in_a_pattern_are_plain_text`), never a regex. `{{Step.data.field}}` (and `{{item.field}}`) is `engine.field_ref` / `read_field`; a missing field is `checks.missing_values`, clipped data is `checks.unreadable_values` ("the data was too large to read a field from").
  THE DOORS. `checks.step_problem` (still the ONE function every door that saves calls) is now `validate.problems(...)[0]`, which walks into blocks (`steps[i].steps[j] (label): …`; `lib/workflowStepProblems.stepProblemOf` opens the block and names the step) and adds: no condition / no list / an empty block / too deep / a limit out of range / an ask in a For each with `parallel` > 1 / a group or Retry on a block / two steps of one name in a block's list / `{{item}}` outside a For each / a value from a step that runs LATER, from a step inside a block this step is not in (use `{{Block}}`), from the If's other lane, or from the step itself / a step named `<block>/…` (it would be taken for a step inside that block). `create_record` asks `problems(structure_only=True)` (`BlockRefused`, "This workflow cannot run: …"), so an older workflow is refused for nothing new. `validate.BLOCKS_FOR_MODELS` is the ONE text that tells a model about the blocks: chat's `workflow_draft` spec (both lanes; `tests/fixtures/harness_off_golden_v1366.json` regenerated for it), `workflow_create` and `POST /workflows/generate`; `_sanitize_draft` keeps a block's fields and lists (12 a list, 3 deep).
  THE CANVAS. A block is a container node (`each`, `if`; `components/workflow/blocks.ts`): its steps are child nodes (`parentId`, `branch`, `order`; not draggable until 09-b) laid out by `layoutBlocks`, serialized by `branch` and `order`, never by position; `BlockInspector` is the three-field check and the list and limits; Add step with a block (or a step in one) selected adds inside (`addStepInside`). `BlockRunDetail` draws a For each's rows and an If's lane in Run history and the live strip; the draft card lists a block's steps and says `EACH_COST_LINE` for a For each with an Agent step (D-09.1). "loop" and "branch" are retired on the workflow surfaces (`retiredWords.isWorkflowSurface`). Not in 09-a: dragging steps in and out (09-b), "Wait until" (09-c), a rehearsal of blocks (06-b), a step count that counts the steps inside a block (the saved row and the load banner say "1 step" for a For each of four steps; 09-b). Pins: `tests/test_leap09a_{logic,for_each,if,ask_in_block,validate,tool_gate}.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/leap-09a-blocks.test.tsx`.
  THE REVIEW'S FIXES. A resume also reaches a block that FINISHED failed (a failure skipped past, or one inside an If's lane skipped past), so: a For each that ends `failed` keeps `list` and `found` and is RETURNED AS IT IS when reached again (never listed again, so no result lands on another file; it drops them only when it completes); a For each that finds the row that STOPPED it runs no item after it (one before it that was under way, several at once, is finished): a row is written `halts` only when the item's failure was not skipped past inside it (an inner step's own skip leaves it off, so the block goes on past that item after a restart too), and `bound` when a limit was reached inside it; `halts` stops a block set to stop, `bound` any block; an If keeps `took` (and `took_words`) when it ended `failed` and never decides again. A folder whose `list_folder` scan was cut short (`scan_capped`) or that holds more matching entries than one listing shows (`FOLDER_LIST_CAP`, 1,000) stops the block BEFORE any item (`folder_unlisted_words`), WHATEVER the limit (`list_folder` keeps the largest files, so a part of a listing is not the first files by name); `validate.FOLDER_ITEMS_CAP` (1,000) refuses a higher `max_items` over a folder, and the panel's field stops there. While a For each works its line counts only what is settled ("6 of 14 done"). An If that took Otherwise says what was true (`logic.NOT_WORDS`: "Otherwise: “4,999.99” is not over “5000”."), never the comparison that failed as if it held (seen in Run history on a scratch daemon). `_sanitize_draft` (`_draft_kind`) reads "for-each", "foreach", "forEach", "For each", "if-else" as the block they are and keeps any other unknown kind AS WRITTEN, so the save check refuses it by name; the draft card shows it as "Unknown step". `workflow_create`'s result says `EACH_COST_LINE` (`workflows/tools.each_cost_note`), and the card's cost line walks into If lanes (`blocks.eachHoldsAgent`). `BLOCKS_FOR_MODELS` and the block fields' descriptions are kept short: they go out with every request that offers those doors (`test_agent_too_small_v14210`, `test_reply_budget_v1387`).
  REVIEW 2. A For each's items are `outside` when any value its list is made from is, found the way the save check finds a reference's step (`validate._ref_base`: `{{item.sub}}` reads `item`, so a nested For each over a field of an item from `{{Trigger}}` or a folder is fenced too; the reference as written is read as well). A rule's start (`reflex/router`) and a schedule's fire (`platform._run_scheduled_workflow`, `BlockRefused` as `_ScheduleRefused`) say an `UnknownStepKind` or a `BlockRefused` in its own sentence, never "UnknownStepKind: …" or the generic "couldn't start this task". Pins: `test_leap09a_for_each.py::test_a_for_each_over_a_field_of_an_outside_item_is_fenced_too`, `test_an_item_an_inner_skip_went_past_does_not_stop_the_block_after_a_resume`, `test_a_limit_reached_inside_an_item_stops_a_skipping_block_after_a_resume_too`, `test_an_item_that_reached_a_limit_is_written_as_the_one_that_stopped_the_block`, `test_a_folder_bigger_than_one_listing_is_never_worked_through_in_part` (a lower limit and files of different sizes), `test_leap09a_validate.py::test_a_stored_workflow_a_rule_or_a_schedule_cannot_run_is_said_in_its_own_sentence`; every guard mutation-checked red.
  REVIEW 3. A line that QUOTES outside words is outside words: an If whose condition reads an outside value (`engine._reads_outside`, the same reading as a For each's list), an If or a For each whose line carries an inner step's outside failure, a For each with an outside row, a For each that could not start on an outside value ("… is not a list (it gave …)"), and a notify whose message read one ("notified: …", delivered as written) are marked `outside`; the mark is kept on a running If (a resume reads it), on an item's short copy and on its rows. An agent step gets each of them FENCED by every route: `{{Check}}`, `[step Check failed: …]`, `{{Each.data}}`, and "Context from earlier steps" (`_completed_chain` and `_local_chain` pass the mark; `_context_block` fences that summary). Pins: the "Outside words an If (or a message) quotes" tests in `test_leap09a_if.py`; every guard mutation-checked red.
  REVIEW 4. A TOOL step whose tool `returns_untrusted_content` (`read_file`, `read_document`, `extract_pdf`, `shell`…) and whose result is not `is_own_source` has its output marked `outside` (`_run_tool_step`), so `{{Read}}`, `{{Read.data.x}}`, an If or a For each built on it and "Context from earlier steps" reach an agent step fenced, at the top level and inside a block (was OPEN since review 2). `/workflows/generate` reads the model's reply with `core/jsonish.loads_object` (`_extract_workflow_json` is now a thin wrapper over it, for the chat-to-workflow route), and its one repair round says the step kinds and `BLOCKS_FOR_MODELS`, so a restated workflow keeps its blocks. `workflow_run` says an `UnknownStepKind` in its own sentence. Pins: `test_leap09a_validate.py::test_the_builder_reads_a_near_json_reply_with_blocks_in_one_model_call`, `test_the_builder_s_restatement_round_keeps_the_blocks`, `test_the_chat_tool_that_runs_a_stored_workflow_says_an_unknown_kind_in_its_own_sentence`; `test_leap09a_if.py::test_what_a_tool_read_from_a_file_reaches_a_later_agent_step_fenced` (6 mutations red).
- **A workflow or a goal is rehearsed through its OWN engine with the rehearsal on its record, and the report says where a rehearsal stops being the real run: at the workflow's question, and at a read after a held change** (v1.596.0, idea 06, phase 06-b; master plan R3.2).
  THE DOOR. `tools/rehearsal_runs.start(kind="workflow"|"goal")` (the page's `POST /rehearsals`, chat's `rehearse`). A WORKFLOW: `WorkflowEngine.create_record(wf, started_by=person, rehearsal_id=<rehearsal>)` (the real run's own checks refuse first) stores `WorkflowRunRecord.rehearsal_id` (additive), and `run_record` reads it from the record into `engine._rehearsals`; `rehearsal_of(run_id)` is the ONE question every step asks. A tool step passes it in its `ToolContext` (the registry holds every call that is not a read, 06-a's gate); a tool the tier refuses is still RECORDED as refused through the registry's deny seam (only in a rehearsal; a real run is unchanged); `_run_notify_step` records `SIDE_DOORS["workflow_notify"]` and sends nothing; an `ask` ENDS the run (`_rehearse_ask`: one `workflow_ask` row, "ask you: <question>", with `after` = what was not rehearsed, innermost first, read from `ask.at` and a For each's stored list by `_after_ask`); an agent step's session gets `options={"rehearsal_id": …}` and NO other change (same agent, `provider=None` as the real step: the same model and account). A rehearsal's run publishes NO workflow event (`_publish`), is never set up from a chat (so `_report_end` writes nothing), writes no record of checks (`_note_expect_check`), judges no expectation of a held step (`out["rehearsed"]`), removes its scratch folder, is left out of `GET /workflows/runs` and `/runs`, and is refused by Resume (409). Its tool events carry the RUN's id, so `rehearsal.session_is_rehearsal` also reads `WorkflowRunRecord.rehearsal_id` (an outgoing webhook on `tool.executed` hears nothing of it); the report lists every webhook on the workflow's own events. Blocks (If, For each) need nothing of their own: they run through the same `_exec_step`. A workflow of tool, notify and ask steps is rehearsed with ZERO model calls (release 11 of the intelligence plan builds on that: pinned by `tests/test_leap06b_workflow.py`, whose model double fails the test if called). The rehearsal settles from the RUN RECORD (`_settle_workflow`: finished → ready, a halting step → failed in that step's words, cancelled → stopped, unfinished with no driver → failed "when Iron Jarvis restarted"); Stop cancels the driver (`_drive_workflow`), which ends the run `cancelled`.
  A GOAL: `GoalEngine.run_iteration(goal_id, rehearsal=<id>)` → `_rehearse_try`: the real try's gates refuse in the same words (state other than active or paused, the deny floor, a spent budget, Emergency stop) but publish nothing and report nowhere; the try's session carries the rehearsal and `local_only` when the goal's chat is Local only, and NOT `chat_thread_id`; a goal that reports to a chat gets one `chat_delivery` rehearsed row instead. It settles no spend, writes no checkpoint (not even `running_session_id`), records no success or failure on the breaker, moves no state, publishes no `goal.*` event, and runs no checks or judge. Pinned by `tests/test_leap06b_goal.py` (budget, checkpoint, breaker, state and `last_run_at` equal before and after, with the real try as the control).
  THE LIMITS, by code from the ledger: `report()` reads the rows of the workflow's run id too; `stopped_at {question, not_rehearsed}` and `stopped_words` come from the `workflow_ask` row; `guessed_after` (`rehearsal.guessed_after`, every subject kind) is true when a held change (never an ask, never `AFTER_THE_RUN`: a delivery, a webhook, a lesson, a chat report, which a rehearsal writes before its run) came before a read that RAN (a read that failed counts: the file a held write would have made), with `GUESSED_AFTER_WORDS`. Pinned by `tests/test_leap06b_guessed_after.py`. Keep it stamps `rehearsed_at` on `WorkflowRecord` (by id) and `GoalContractRecord` (additive). OPEN: a held write whose path the real tool would refuse (outside its folder) is still listed as "would write" (the confinement check is inside the tool's execute, after the hold); a workflow that takes run inputs is rehearsed without them; a schedule or a rule that starts a workflow or a goal is still refused ("cannot be rehearsed yet") rather than rehearsed through this door.
